long.extra_condition: AND close[1] was below the Fibo level by SafetyBuffer. Applied to any of: Fibo76, Fibo61, Fibo38, Fibo23. TrendDirection must be 1 (up).

custom_logic_notes: The EA uses ZigZag pivot points to identify the last 4 swing highs/lows (HL[0..3]). Trend is determined by comparing alternating pivots: if HL[0]>HL[2] and HL[1]>HL[3] then uptrend; if HL[0]<HL[2] and HL[1]<HL[3] then downtrend. Fibonacci retracement levels are drawn on the most recent ZigZag leg. Entry triggers when current bar close crosses above a Fibonacci level while the previous bar close was below it (for buys in uptrend) or vice versa (for sells in downtrend), with a SafetyBuffer threshold. A CloseBarPause prevents re-entry for N bars after a position is closed by stop-loss. The CheckTrend function return type is declared as bool but returns int values (0, 1, -1), which is a bug but works due to implicit conversion. The TradeCheck function uses deal=1 for Buy but case 2 for Sell, while the caller passes -1 for Sell, so the Sell path is never executed in TradeCheck — this is a bug. The Fibonacci object (MyFIBO) is created/updated on each qualifying tick as a chart object.
python_conversion_notes: Key challenges: (1) ZigZag indicator must be reimplemented or sourced as a Python equivalent since it uses iCustom with Examples\ZigZag path. (2) Fibonacci level calculation depends on the last 4 ZigZag pivots which must be tracked statefully. (3) The entry logic compares current bar close vs previous bar close against Fibonacci levels with SafetyBuffer in points — requires careful point/pip normalization. (4) The CloseBarPause mechanism tracks bars since last SL close using OnTrade history — must be replicated via trade history tracking. (5) Bug: TradeCheck Sell case uses case 2 but is called with -1, meaning sell orders never actually execute via TradeCheck — needs decision on whether to fix or replicate the bug. (6) CheckTrend return type mismatch (bool returning int) works in MQL5 but must use int in Python. (7) No new-bar guard on signal evaluation — signals are checked every tick, meaning the Fibonacci crossover condition could trigger on intrabar price movement; for backtesting, bar-close evaluation is recommended.
